files.role: Workspace-inheriting package manifest for internal table-format utilities, with optional DynamoDB and vendored-protoc integration.
ranges: Package name is lance-table; version, edition, authors, license, repository, keywords, categories and minimum Rust version inherit workspace values. README.md and the utility description are local. This file does not establish the inherited version numbers.

Runtime dependencies link Arrow family types/IPC and the lance-arrow/core/file/select/io crates, plus async-trait. Each declaration uses the workspace dependency; actual use sites require their corresponding source analysis.

AWS credential/DynamoDB dependencies are optional. DynamoDB explicitly disables default features and requests default-https-client plus rt-tokio. Remaining workspace dependencies provide BLAKE3, bytes/byte order, time, futures/logging, object store, protobuf/types, randomness, ranges/bitmaps, serde/JSON, semver/Snafu, Tokio/tracing, URL and UUID. Pins are in the still-pending root workspace/lockfiles.
Dev dependencies use workspace datagen/testing plus arrow-schema, criterion, pretty_assertions, proptest and rstest. Their presence does not prove any tests have executed.
prost-build is a build dependency. Optional protobuf-src is selected by protoc; dynamodb selects both optional AWS dependencies and lance-io/aws. There is no default feature list in this manifest.
docs.rs builds request protoc; the comment attributes this to an older Ubuntu protoc. This is a declared docs build setting, not current docs.rs environment verification.
Three separate harness=false Criterion-style bench targets are named row_id_index, manifest_intern and system_columns. Source and actual measurement behavior are separate files.
The fourth harness=false target is version_columns. Workspace lints are inherited. No ad hoc profile override is declared here.

files.role: Cargo build script generating table protobuf Rust bindings.
ranges: License/import prelude and main returning std::io::Result. Cargo is told to rerun the build script when protos changes; generated output is consumed by format::pb.

With feature protoc, an unsafe block sets the build process PROTOC environment variable to protobuf_src::protoc(). Without that feature this assignment is compiled out. This is build-time configuration, not a runtime table option.

Prost maps the .lance.file package to ::lance_file::format::pb, enables proto3 optional support and type names, and maps DataFragment.inline_row_ids to Bytes. The comment motivates zero-copy slices and reports a roughly98% large-manifest share; the percentage is an unmeasured source-comment claim, while the configuration itself is explicit.

Compile table.proto, transaction.proto and rowids.proto with ./protos include directory, propagate compilation IO errors with ?, then return Ok. No checked-in generated output or successful compilation is established by reading this script.

files.role: Public metadata facade, generated table bindings, manifest footer identifiers and UUID conversions.
ranges: Imports Arrow byte-slice conversion and UUID. fragment, index, manifest, row_ids and transaction are private child modules, while key_existence and overlay are public. Visibility of reexported types is determined by the following explicit facade declarations.

Reexports the three row dataset-version types from rowids::version; every public fragment item; IndexFile/IndexMetadata/index_metadata_codec/list_index_files_with_sizes; the listed manifest/version/schema-reader helpers; external/inline row-id types and reserved field IDs; Transaction and operation_may_change_schema. Private-module paths themselves remain inaccessible externally. Definitions and algorithms in the target files remain pending.

Uses core Error/Result. Public Index aliases IndexMetadata with deprecated(since=0.36.1, note=Use IndexMetadata instead); the preceding comment attributes the rename to trait-name conflicts. No wrapper object or conversion is introduced.

Public pb module includes OUT_DIR/lance.table.rs generated during the build. Generated code relaxes the named Clippy/naming/unused/improper_ctypes lints locally. The module contains no handwritten wire definitions.

Manifest footer identifiers are signed i16 MAJOR_VERSION=0, MINOR_VERSION=1 and four-byte MAGIC=LANC. These are table-manifest identifiers; this file does not specify footer byte order or data-file v2 version handling.

TryFrom<&pb::Uuid> for uuid::Uuid rejects lengths other than16 with InvalidInput text Protobuf UUID is malformed. Otherwise copies bytes into a stack [u8;16] and constructs Uuid::from_bytes. It validates length, not UUID version/variant semantics.
From<&Uuid> for pb::Uuid copies the UUID bytes into a new Vec field. Conversion is infallible and does not parse or format a textual UUID.

files.role: Iterator extension attaching caller-supplied exact remaining size; also exposes stream utilities.
ranges: SPDX prelude, public stream module and public LanceIteratorExtension trait. exact_size consumes Sized self and returns ExactSize<Self>; the trait declaration itself does not require Iterator.
Blanket implementation for every Iterator stores the original iterator and caller-provided usize size without counting or validation. No iteration or collection happens at construction.
ExactSize<I> is a public wrapper with private inner and size fields. Documentation motivates flatten-style precomputed sizes and links an upstream discussion; that URL was not accessed.

Iterator forwards Item. next polls inner, leaves size unchanged on None, and decrements by1 for every Some. The caller must supply the true remaining count: too small can underflow (panic when overflow checks apply, otherwise wrap); too large remains overreported even after inner exhaustion. No fused guarantee is added.

size_hint returns (size,Some(size)) unconditionally; ExactSizeIterator is implemented without overriding len or adding checks. This declaration trusts the constructor count and does not independently enforce the exact-size contract.

files.role: Table capability bits, support gates, mutable flag reconstruction and local source tests.
ranges: SPDX/module prelude imports Manifest and core Error/Result; all feature logic operates on manifest fields or explicit u64 words.

Bits0..5 are deletion files, stable row IDs, deprecated v2-format marker, table config, base paths and disable transaction file. Comments distinguish stable row identity from physical addresses and describe writer-only inline-transaction preference. The deprecated v2 bit is retained for recognition, not emitted by apply_feature_flags.

Bit6 marks unstable overlays whose ignored updates would expose stale base cells. Documented release opt-in/debug support is implemented by data_overlay_files_enabled below; mere bit definition does not make every build accept it.

Bit7 is covered-index metadata. Comments describe the older trailing-suffix fields contract and why reader and writer fences are needed. Historical claims about reclaimed MemWAL bit7, released unknown boundaries and beta4..17 exposure are recorded as source comments only; they are not verified release compatibility facts.

Bit8 marks mixed recognized v2 exact file versions; bit9 marks stable-row-ID tables with fragment reuse, supported only with debug assertions; bit10 marks tagged fragment-reuse mappings. Comment says legacy-only FRI does not set bit10; the now-reviewed builder sets paired bit10 when final indices contain a tagged entry (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1914-1919).

Bit11 marks row IDs or created/updated dataset-version sequences stored as hidden data columns and has a debug/environment support gate. Comments explain incompatible older oneof interpretation; historical universal rejection claims remain unverified. Bit12 is reserved fragment trees and always rejected by the mask.

Bit13 reserves independent key/covering declarations and documents dependence on covered-index bit7. Implementation explicitly masks it out; this is not an implemented migration/pair-retention policy. FLAG_UNKNOWN is1<<14 (16384), the upper boundary for the initial mask.

Compile-time assertions place covered/mixed/stable-FRI/tagged-FRI/spilled/tree/independent bits below FLAG_UNKNOWN and covered/stable-FRI at minimum historical fence positions7/9. Assertions prove arithmetic positions only. Crate-visible STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS contains exactly mixed bit8 and tagged-FRI bit10, not every paired feature.
Public opt-in variable names are LANCE_ENABLE_UNSTABLE_DATA_OVERLAY_FILES and LANCE_ENABLE_UNSTABLE_SPILLED_ROW_LINEAGE. Their values are not parsed; helpers check var_os presence.

apply_feature_flags first takes the union of either word's covered-index bit and calls validated_sticky_paired_flags. Paired validation failure occurs before mutation. It then zeroes both words. The now-reviewed build_manifest derives covering bits after calling this helper (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1686-1720); the complete dataset write_manifest_file path remains pending.

Any deletion_file sets bit0 in both words. If any fragment has row_id_meta or enable_stable_row_id is true, every fragment must have row IDs, otherwise InvalidInput All fragments must have row ids. Empty fragments satisfy all vacuously and can enable stable mode. A failure here happens after reset and possible deletion-bit writes, so this function is not rollback-atomic. On success stable bit1 is set in both.

Nonempty config sets table-config bit3 only in writer word. Nonempty base_paths sets bit4 in both (not a check that length exceeds1). Any nonempty overlays list sets unstable overlay bit6 in both, without consulting the current support gate.

Any frag.has_spilled_row_lineage() sets bit11 in both; detector internals are pending. disable_transaction_file sets writer bit5 only. Finally restore covered bit7 into both words and validated sticky bits8/10 into both, then Ok. Other incoming bits including deprecated v2, unknown/reserved and stable-FRI bit9 are cleared unless derived elsewhere; this routine does not itself ensure reader/writer support.

inherit_sticky_feature_flags validates source paired bits before any destination write, then ORs bits8/10 into both destination words. It preserves unrelated destination bits and does not validate destination, transfer covered metadata or infer capabilities from fragment contents.

Overlay and spilled-lineage helpers return cfg!(debug_assertions) OR environment-variable presence; empty/non-Unicode/0 strings count as present, no cached OnceLock. Overlay helper is private; spilled helper is public. Hidden public stable-row-ID FRI helper returns only cfg!(debug_assertions), with no environment override. Build-profile labels in prose are shorthand; actual predicate is debug_assertions.

mark_supported only clears the supplied bit when disabled. supported_flags_when starts at FLAG_UNKNOWN-1 and clears overlay/stable-FRI/spilled bits according to three booleans, then always clears tree and independent covering. It recognizes all other bits below14, including deprecated v2 and writer-specific bits, without enforcing semantic combinations.

supported_flags reads the three current gates each call. can_read_dataset and can_write_dataset accept when their given word contains no unsupported bits; both use the identical support mask. Zero is accepted; these word-only checks do not inspect the counterpart word, contents or per-file versions.

ensure_can_read_manifest/ensure_can_write_manifest first validate paired bits, then check only the relevant feature word. Unsupported flags return NotSupported via not_supported_source with the decimal flags and upgrade prompt. Corrupt paired errors take precedence. These are capability checks, not content/version/format validation.

has_deprecated_v2_feature_flag is a bit2 test. validate_paired_feature_flags first rejects XOR disagreement in tagged-FRI bit10 with CorruptFile named manifest, then mixed bit8 disagreement with another CorruptFile. No other bits are paired-validated here. validated_sticky_paired_flags calls that validator and returns reader word masked by bits8/10.

Test module gated cfg(test). tagged_fri_flag_is_supported_and_sticky asserts word acceptance, reader-only tagged-FRI rejection and preservation of both after apply. It does not exercise actual FRI decoding.

Covered-metadata test asserts bit128 and present-build read/write acceptance. Comments about older release refusal are not backed by loading a historical fixture here. Test imports super::* and BasePath.

Fragment-tree test checks4096, separation from FRI bits and read/write refusal. Stable-row-ID FRI test checks512, uses explicit policy booleans for exclusion/inclusion and unrelated-bit rejection, then compares both word gates with the actual debug predicate. No build profiles or environment variables are changed.

Independent-covering test asserts8192 and refusal of its union with bit7. Reader test accepts zero, known bits0..5, a combined subset and current overlay policy; rejects FLAG_UNKNOWN. These checks do not validate individual manifest contents.

Overlay policy test compares disabled/enabled masks while retaining deletion support. Spilled policy test checks2048, exclusion/inclusion and retention of mixed-version support. Historical boundary commentary remains unverified; tests pass explicit booleans rather than mutate process environment.

Overlay derivation fixture builds a one-field Int64 schema, one fragment and a dense overlay backed by the legacy-named DataFile constructor, then asserts overlay bit in both words after apply. This uses in-memory metadata, not a written overlay data file.

Spilled-lineage fixture loops over row ID Column, created-version Column and updated-version Column, using a hidden-row-ID-field DataFile. Each fragment otherwise has inline row IDs so the stable-ID all-fragments check passes. Applying with stable IDs enabled must set spilled bit in both words; no hidden-column reader is exercised.
Inline-only row-ID metadata fixture applies stable mode and checks reader spilled bit remains zero. It does not assert writer spilled bit separately in this case.
Writer counterpart accepts zero, known bits0..5, a multi-bit subset and gated overlay; rejects FLAG_UNKNOWN. Like reader checks, this is word-level policy only.

Base-path derivation compares empty map versus a single BasePath entry with file URI/reference. Empty sets neither bit and one entry sets both. The fixture confirms nonempty-map semantics rather than requiring multiple entries or doing filesystem IO.

Inheritance test ORs a fully paired mixed-version capability into an empty destination and asserts both. Half-set-source test tries both reader-only and writer-only mixed bit and expects an only one of diagnostic; it does not explicitly assert destination nonmutation.

Apply preserves fully paired mixed bit across reset; reader-only apply yields CorruptFile plus diagnostic. Separate paired-validation test covers both mixed half-set orientations. Tests do not imply every flag must be paired.

Writer-gate fixture accepts paired mixed capability, then adds writer unknown bit and asserts NotSupported/cannot be written. empty_manifest creates an Int32 i schema with no fragments/base paths and default storage format.

Final test accepts covered and mixed bits for read/write and rejects unknown for read. Module closes. All source assertions were read, not executed; no file-format compatibility fixture or end-to-end commit occurs here.
